details: The zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the x-coordinates of the points where y = p(x) intersects the x-axis.
A polynomial of degree n can have at most n real zeroes.
Quadratic polynomial y = ax^2 + bx + c forms a parabola opening upwards if a > 0 and downwards if a < 0.
evidence_or_examples: A parabola intersecting x-axis at (-2, 0) and (4, 0) has zeroes -2 and 4.
Cubic graph cutting x-axis at 3 distinct points has 3 real zeroes.

details: For ax^2 + bx + c with zeroes α and β:
Sum of zeroes: α + β = -b/a = -(coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x^2)
Product of zeroes: αβ = c/a = (constant term) / (coefficient of x^2)
evidence_or_examples: For x^2 - 2x - 8, zeroes are 4 and -2: Sum = 2 = -(-2)/1; Product = -8 = -8/1.
Polynomial formation: p(x) = k[x^2 - (α + β)x + αβ].

details: For ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d with zeroes α, β, γ:
Sum of zeroes: α + β + γ = -b/a
Sum of products in pairs: αβ + βγ + γα = c/a
Product of zeroes: αβγ = -d/a
evidence_or_examples: For x^3 - 3x^2 + x + 1 with zeroes a-b, a, a+b: Sum = 3a = 3 => a = 1; Product = a(a^2 - b^2) = -1 => b = ±√2.
